 EIA Now Sees Global Oil Glut in Q4
 by  Andreas Exarheas | Rigzone Staff  | Monday, November 16, 2026 | 7:04 AM EST 
 The U.S. Energy Information Administration now sees a global oil glut this quarter. 
 Image by Yutthana Gaetgeaw via iStock 
 The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) revealed in its latest short term energy outlook (STEO), which was released on November 10, that it now sees an average global oil glut, whereby production exceeds demand, of 1.46 million barrels per day stretching across the fourth quarter of 2026.
 In its previous STEO, which was released in October, the EIA projected a global oil crunch, whereby demand exceeds production, of 0.69 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter.
 The EIA’s latest STEO sees world petroleum and other liquid fuels production averaging 105.14 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter and world petroleum and other liquid fuels demand coming in at 103.67 million barrels per day during the same period. In its previous STEO, the EIA projected that production would average 102.97 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter and demand would average 103.66 million barrels per day.
 Overall in 2026, the EIA still predicts an oil crunch, albeit a tightening one.
 In its latest STEO, the EIA projects a crunch of 0.69 million barrels per day for the year. This marks an almost 50 percent drop to the EIA’s 2026 crunch projection in October, which stood at 1.34 million barrels per day.
 The EIA sees world petroleum and other liquid fuels production coming in at 101.69 million barrels per day and demand averaging 102.38 million barrels per day overall in 2026, in its November STEO. Its previous STEO projected that output would land at 101.09 million barrels per day and demand would average 102.43 million barrels per day.
 2027 
 Advertisement - Scroll to continue 
 Looking ahead to 2027, the EIA’s latest STEO expects an overall oil glut of 4.05 million barrels per day for the year. The EIA’s previous STEO also expected a glut for 2027, albeit a bigger one, at 4.91 million barrels per day.
 In its November STEO, the EIA expects production to average 108.40 million barrels per day and demand to average 104.35 million barrels per day in 2027. The EIA’s October STEO saw output at 109.55 million barrels per day and demand at 104.64 million barrels per day next year.
 A quarterly breakdown included in the EIA’s latest STEO shows that the organization is predicting a global glut of 3.18 million barrels per day in the first quarter of 2027, 3.91 million barrels per day in the second quarter, 4.07 million barrels per day in the third quarter, and 5.02 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter.
 The global oil market saw an average glut of 1.88 million barrels per day in 2025, the EIA’s November STEO showed.
 “We estimate that global oil inventories fell by an average of 1.2 million barrels per day in the third quarter of 2026  but will begin building in the fourth quarter of 2026,” the EIA stated in its November STEO.
 “Although we forecast that global oil production will outpace consumption in 4Q26, the heightened risk of supply disruptions and longer shipping routes will limit the near-term impact of global stock builds until geopolitical risk dissipates and inventories begin to return closer to pre-conflict levels,” it added.
 “We assume export workarounds from the Middle East such as pipeline and overland bypass routes, ship-to-ship transfers, and new pipeline capacity expected to come online in 2027 in the United Arab Emirates will lead to shut-in volumes gradually falling through the Short-Term Energy Outlook forecast period,” the EIA continued.
 “Global inventories in our forecast build by 3.5 million barrels per day in the first half of 2027, pushing the Brent price below $90 per barrel in the second quarter of 2027. We expect the majority of production in the Middle East, outside of Iran, to return to pre-conflict averages by the end of the second quarter of 2027,” it went on to state.
 The EIA highlighted, however, that it expects exports from Iran to remain constrained through the forecast period.
 “As depleted global oil inventories build throughout next year, oil prices gradually fall to an average of $77 per barrel in the fourth quarter of 2027,” it said.
 “However, we expect crude oil flows from the Middle East - via both the Strait of Hormuz and alternative routes - will remain susceptible to disruption, resulting in more volatility in short-term price movements than our monthly forecast indicates,” the EIA warned.
